back: Chimurenga (Shona) and Umvukela (Ndebele) are words for a struggle or rising; the First Chimurenga/Umvukela is the risings of the 1890s.
A person believed to be chosen by a spirit, such as a mhondoro, who speaks for the spirit and guides the community.

front: Who were the two mediums in Mashonaland executed in April 1898?

back: A Mwari priest associated with the Matopo shrines, remembered as a religious figure in the resistance.

front: Where are the Mwari shrines of Njelele and Matonjeni?
back: In the Matopo Hills of Matabeleland.

front: Which cattle disease of 1896 added to the distress?
Why was land a religious matter in 1896?
back: Land was believed to belong to the ancestors and territorial spirits and to hold graves and shrines, so defending it was a duty.

front: Why did people follow the mediums?
back: They believed the spirit spoke through the medium, so the message carried the authority of the ancestors.

front: How do historians disagree about the risings?
back: Some say the Mwari cult and the mediums coordinated them; others stress local grievances and local leaders; a balanced view gives religion an important but not the only part.
